name: Giralda
aka: minaret of the Great Mosque of Seville

dates.altered: The Renaissance belfry added over the second shaft after the 1356 earthquake brought down the original finial; the mosque it served was replaced by the Gothic cathedral from 1401.
dates.note: The article states that construction of the minaret began in 1184 under Ben Ahmad Baso and that, per the chronicler Ibn Sahib al-Salah, 'the works were completed on 10 March 1198'.

refs.title: Seville Cathedral - Wikipedia
refs.note: Carried because it prints a SECOND and different set of figures for the same tower: 'its square base is 7.0 m (23 ft) above sea level and 13 m (44 ft) long per side' and 'The total height of the Giralda tower from the ground to the weather vane is 104.5 m (342 ft 10 in)'. The Giralda article gives the base as 13.6 m. Neither is changed.

survey.prepared: No revision date was printed in the extract. AN ENCYCLOPEDIA ARTICLE AND NOT A REGISTER; the article's own citation for the fifteenth-century plan of the cathedral is Ruiz and Jiménez Martín, 'A Fifteenth-Century Plan of the Cathedral of Seville', Architectural History 55 (2012), 57-77, which was not read here.

quotes.text: The base at street level is a square of 13.6 m (45 ft) on the side and which sits on a solid foundation which is a bit wider, 15–16 m (49.21–52.49 ft) and about 5 m (16 ft) deep. The foundation is built with solid, rectangular stones, some taken and reused from the nearby walls of the former Abbadid palace and from the Roman city walls.
quotes.page: English Wikipedia, section on the minaret; the sentence is followed in the extract by the marker '[citation needed]'

quotes.text: The tower consists of two sections: the main shaft and a much smaller second shaft, superimposed on top of it, which is enveloped today by the Renaissance-era belfry. The main shaft is 50.51 m (165.7 ft) tall and the second shaft is 14.39 m (47.2 ft) tall and has a square base measuring 6.83 m (22.4 ft).
quotes.page: English Wikipedia, section on the minaret

quotes.text: It had a rectangular floor plan measuring approximately 113 by 135 meters. The prayer hall was symmetrical and airy, with a still-extant courtyard, the Patio de los Naranjos, or "Courtyard of Orange Trees."
quotes.page: English Wikipedia, section on the Great Mosque of Seville that the minaret served
